newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to March 7.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to March 7.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of March 7 were $10.519 billion, compared to $10.472 billion on Feb. 28.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of March 7 were $20.339 billion, compared to $20.202 billion as of Feb. 28.
The central bank said the increase of $47 million in net international assets in the same time period was due to:
--Net income from operations by the state oil company Pemex worth $102 million.
--Net sales of foreign currency to the federal government worth $5.0 million.

--A let loss of $50 million dollars for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that between February 28 and March 7 the monetary base fell by 1.863 billion pesos due to a fall in the seasonal demand of bills and coins.
During the week, deposits of the federal government fell 862 million pesos, due to the net results of government expenses less tax collections.
To avoid an excess of liquidity due to the operations of the federal government and other factors, Banco de Mexico said it had received deposits worth 4.001 billion pesos from financial institutes.

*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
